options: The policy whose value function is being estimated
The policy actually used to generate actions and collect experience in the environment
The optimal policy derived from Q*
A policy that never changes during training
questions.explain: The behavior policy is the one actually generating the agent's actions as it interacts with the environment — often an exploratory policy like epsilon-greedy.

options: It never uses a discount factor
The behavior policy and the target policy are the same (or forced to stay close)
It only works in episodic tasks
It uses a replay buffer of old experience
questions.explain: On-policy methods learn about the value of the exact policy that is generating the data; behavior policy and target policy coincide.

questions.q: In SARSA's update rule, what makes it on-policy?
options: It uses max_a Q(S_{t+1}, a) in the update
It uses the next action A_{t+1} actually selected by the agent's own behavior policy in the update
It never uses a learning rate α
It ignores the reward signal
questions.explain: SARSA's update plugs in Q(S_{t+1}, A_{t+1}) where A_{t+1} is the action actually taken next by the current (exploratory) policy — learning the value of the policy actually being followed.

options: It uses max_a Q(S_{t+1}, a) — the best possible next action — rather than the action the agent actually took
It requires on-policy data collection
It cannot use epsilon-greedy exploration
It does not use a reward signal
questions.explain: Q-learning bootstraps using max_a Q(S_{t+1}, a), the value of the greedy target policy, regardless of which action the exploratory behavior policy actually chose — the two policies differ.

questions.q: Why can off-policy methods like Q-learning reuse old experience (e.g. via a replay buffer) more easily than strictly on-policy methods?
options: Off-policy methods don't require data to come from the exact policy currently being evaluated, so data from an older or different policy is still usable
Off-policy methods don't use value functions
On-policy methods require more memory than off-policy methods
Replay buffers only work with continuing tasks
questions.explain: Because off-policy learning estimates the value of a target policy different from whatever generated the data, it can reuse transitions collected under older policies, enabling experience replay.
